output:
I need to get my bearings here. Taxes due, no food in the house, and the government's coffers sitting empty while seats go vacant. That's the ledger I'm waking up to.

First thing's first - seeing what I owe and what's coming at me. Then I need to figure if mining today will cover the day's bleed.  Ledger's clean on personal debts, but that doesn't include today's taxes or upkeep. I see what's shaping up.

Let me get my head around what primitives I can actually call and what they'll cost me. Every move I make today needs to pencil out. I see my situation clearly now. Standing at home:h34, nobody here, and the day's ledger already ticking against me. 120 sim due today - 90 for the household's upkeep, 30 for my head tax. I've got 5000 sim in hand, which sounds ample until you count how fast it drains while you're still figuring out which end of the pick to hold.

The Kasukabe Ore Outcrop is where I need to be. Mining costs 8 sim per unit minimum - 5 for tool wear plus the base. But I need to know what the market's paying for ore before I commit my morning to hauling rock that's worthless.

Let me move to the ore outcrop and see what's waiting there. If copper's running, I'll know what to price it at.  So I'm walking - nine ticks by the town's reckoning. That's nine ticks of being unable to earn, nine ticks of burning toward the day's taxes without income. That's fair. The ledger doesn't care how far the outcrop sits from your door.

I'm wondering what ores are pulling, what the vein's showing. And what Ezra Okonjo might have posted. He works ore or nobody does, per the town's description, but hasn't figured what ore costs here. That tells me the market's unsettled - prices fluctuating, or nobody's yet written the price that clears demand.

Let me reach the outcrop and look around. Then I'll mine, enough to cover today and leave margin for tomorrow. The outcrop's at Kasukabe Ore Outcrop, and I need to be there to mine. Already walking - 9 ticks estimated. I've burned costs already without earning. The ledger tightens. I need to arrive and assess what's mineable before committing picks to stone.

I'll make do with what the day hands me. That's all any miner can promise.   Right. I'm still at home:h34, haven't moved an inch, and now the walking's cancelled. The ledger just took 1 sim for that interruption. Small cost, but costs accumulate.

Let me actually move to the ore outcrop this time. That's where my living is.  Walking now—9 ticks to the outcrop. 9 ticks of burning daylight and accumulating costs while no ore fills my pockets. That's the physics of it. I'll arrive, look around to see what ores are running and who's buying, and then get to work.

The day's already ticking against me. 120 sim due, and every tick of walking is a tick of earning lost. But that's the price of distance—payable in time, not coin.

Let me let the walk complete next turn. No need to keep burning sim on rest stops. Just walk until I get there. Walking takes time. I'll let this tick complete and arrive at the outcrop next turn. 9 ticks of walking, burning daylight and accumulating costs with no income. The ledger tightens.

Take the next tick. I'll arrive, survey what's mineable, and start pulling ore that covers today's bleed and builds buffer for tomorrow. Walking now - 9 ticks to the Kasukabe Ore Outcrop. I'll arrive and assess what's pulling from the ground, then get to work. The ledger's already ticking against me.
